about: Which levels of government may set each law amount the engine tracks. A local body also needs its state's grant where the state law says so (checked separately for the minimum wage, income tax and sales tax). Read by draftBill: a bill a body has no power to pass is blocked with the law's reason.

minimum-wage.source: 29 U.S.C. § 206 (federal floor); 29 U.S.C. § 218 (states and places may set higher)

income-tax.source: U.S. Const. amend. XVI; state constitutions; local income taxes only where state law authorizes them

local-income-tax-authority.source: State law decides whether its localities may levy an income tax (Tax Foundation, Local Income Taxes: A Primer, 2023)

sales-tax.source: No federal sales tax; local sales taxes only where state law authorizes them

property-tax.source: Property taxes are levied by local governments under state law (U.S. Const. art. I, § 9 bars an unapportioned federal direct tax)

snap-maximum.source: 7 U.S.C. § 2017 (allotments set federally from the Thrifty Food Plan)

unemployment-weekly-maximum.source: State unemployment insurance law under 26 U.S.C. § 3304

unemployment-insurance.source: State unemployment insurance law under 26 U.S.C. § 3304

public-pay-floor.source: Each government sets its own employees' pay: 5 U.S.C. § 5303 (federal pay schedules), state civil service law, and city and county charters

state-unemployment-tax.source: State unemployment insurance law under 26 U.S.C. § 3304

corporate-income-tax.source: 26 U.S.C. § 11 (federal); state corporate income taxes under state law

estate-tax.source: 26 U.S.C. 2001 (federal estate tax); state estate taxes under each state's taxing power (Tax Foundation, Estate and Inheritance Taxes by State, 2026). No local government levies one.

inheritance-tax.source: State inheritance taxes under each state's taxing power (Ky. Rev. Stat. ch. 140; Md. Tax-Gen. 7-203; Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004; N.J.S.A. 54:34; 72 P.S. 9116). Congress levies none; no local government levies one.

us-policy-positions:agriculture-natural-.source: State water codes; county and district groundwater rules (e.g., groundwater management districts)
State farmland-preservation acts; county agricultural zoning

us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.source: State usury and small-loan acts; federal Military Lending Act (10 U.S.C. sec. 987); local bodies have no usury power

us-policy-positions:business-commerce.le.source: State cannabis acts; local opt-out of retail sales where the state allows it

us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.source: Fair Housing Act and Title VII; state human rights acts; local human rights ordinances
State abortion statutes after Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization (2022); federal bills

us-policy-positions:education.public-fun.source: State voucher and education savings account acts

us-policy-positions:education.universal-.source: State pre-K acts; city and county programs

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.source: Clean Air Act state implementation plans (42 U.S.C. sec. 7410)
State renewable and clean electricity standards

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.p.source: State carbon pricing programs; federal bills

us-policy-positions:fiscal.adopt-income-.source: U.S. Const. amend. XVI; state constitutions (local income tax is the separate local-income-tax series)

us-policy-positions:fiscal.balanced-oper.source: State constitutions and statutes; local charters and budget acts

us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-grocer.source: State sales-tax codes; local sales-tax ordinances where the state lets places set their own base; there is no federal sales tax

us-policy-positions:fiscal.fund-pensions.source: Each government's own pension funding policy

us-policy-positions:government-operation.source: State election codes; National Voter Registration Act
18 U.S.C. sec. 207; state ethics acts; local ethics codes
State constitutions and statutes; city charters for council districts

us-policy-positions:health-human-service.source: Public Law 119-21; state Medicaid plans and waivers; counties administer, never set, eligibility

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.all.source: State zoning-reform acts; local zoning codes

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.inc.source: State housing acts; local inclusionary zoning ordinances

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.ren.source: State rent acts; local rent ordinances where not preempted

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.source: Local ordinances and charters; state oversight acts
State bail statutes and court rules
8 U.S.C. sec. 1357(g); state acts; county sheriff and city agreements
State carry statutes; local firearm laws are generally preempted

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.paid.source: State paid-leave acts; local ordinances (e.g., city paid parental leave); federal bills

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.publ.source: State public-employee bargaining acts; local charters and ordinances

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.rais.source: 29 U.S.C. sec. 206 and 218; state and local wage laws

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.righ.source: 29 U.S.C. sec. 164(b) leaves right-to-work to states

us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.r.source: Local ordinances and state acts on government use

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.source: State road-usage-charge acts; federal pilot programs
State broadband acts; municipal broadband ordinances where not preempted
23 U.S.C. flexible funding; state transportation budgets

questionsAbout: Which levels of government may answer each policy question, ESTIMATED by OPUS-GOV from where such laws are enacted in practice (the cited statutes; NCSL and NLC surveys). A local body also needs the state not to have preempted it (authorityFor). A level not listed has no power to pass the question.
